name: Anchored Subcube-Scaffold Obstructions
statement: For $X=\{a,b,q\}\mathbin{\dot\cup}U$ with $U\ne\varnothing$, let $\mathcal K_d^{\mathrm{an},\delta}$ be obtained from $2^X$ by deleting $\{a\}$, $\{b\}$, all $\{a,b\}\cup T$ for $T\subseteq U$, and optionally $\{a,q\}$ according to $\delta\in\{0,1\}$. It is a learning space rooted at $\{a,b,q\}$. At $\varnothing$ and $X$ its repair sets are $\{a,b,q\}$ and $U\cup\{q\}$ when $\delta=0$, or $U$ when $\delta=1$. Its empty-endpoint pendant extension is a contraction-minimal nonlearning partial cube of order $2^d-2^{d-3}-1-\delta$.
proof: Translation by $\{a,b,q\}$ makes the missing family hereditary in the anchor $q$, which proves union closure, while direct deletion proves accessibility. Rooted-union witnesses determine both endpoint hole sets. Their repair sets cover $X$, so the critical-antipodal pendant criterion gives contraction-minimality; counting the deleted states gives the order.
